binding_note: every piece, sockets included, is a SKINNED mesh on the same 24 bones; the scene binds all of them to the body's Skeleton3D
helmet_on: set to 1 when the helmet is equipped, 0 when removed

shape_key_rules.helmet_on: 1 when the helmet is equipped, 0 when removed
shape_key_rules.grip_R: 1 while the axe is equipped, 0 when not -- closes the right hand round the haft
shape_key_rules.grip_L: 1 while the shield is equipped, 0 when not -- closes the left hand round the grip bar

grip.note: the rig has 24 bones and NO FINGER BONES, so the hands cannot be posed; Meshy ships them open and flat from the A-pose. The weapon BINDING was already rigid -- axe 100% RightHand, shield 100% LeftHand, zero vertices with more than one group, minimum weight 1.0000, verified by reading the exported GLBs back. The open hand was the tell, not the bind.

silhouette_by_facing.instrument: ortho at 52.95 deg, ONE camera scale for every facing, 512 px
silhouette_by_facing.finding: height is near-flat (the scene measured 154-157 px head-to-feet); the difference Matt sees is WIDTH and therefore AREA
silhouette_by_facing.cause: a broad-shouldered figure presents his full shoulder span facing N or S and is edge-on facing E or W. The gear REDUCES the effect -- shield and mantle add bulk to the side views -- so bare is the worst case.

clip_hygiene.defect: the idle clip carried a constant Hips SCALE of 1.176471 = 20/17 exactly -- a 1.70 m source retargeted to a 2.00 m target -- on a rig that is 1.85 m. Hips is the skeleton root, so the whole character was 17.6% bigger whenever he stood still. Present in Meshy's output and carried through T8 and D2 untouched; still present in nb_t8/artifacts/T8-barbarian.glb, which the exporter now neutralises on the way past.

fix.scale_track: Hips scale set to 1.0 at every key in idle
fix.reground: idle root translation.y shifted -16.5286 glTF units (-0.17987 m), ONE constant offset derived from the feet, centred on the loop's min/max so the breathing survives
fix.method: binary accessor patch; the 21 MB texture is never re-encoded

proof_size_is_now_equal.instrument: rigid bone spans -- a uniform scale moves them, no pose can. Silhouette height cannot do this job: at 52.95 deg a vertical metre projects to 0.6025 screen-metres and a FORE-AFT metre to 0.7981, so stride affects screen height more than stature does

grounding.note: walk and run untouched; their renders are byte-identical

standing_height_m.note: the residual idle-to-walk difference is posture: idle pelvis 0.905-0.942 m against walk 0.955-1.034 and rest 1.021. Bone spans are identical, so this is a relaxed stance, not a size change.
